title: Rigveda 5.57: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.57: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.57 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 376v-377v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.57.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 376v
translation.original_text:
1ā ru̍drāsa̱ indra̍vantaḥ sa̱joṣa̍so̱ hira̍ṇyarathāḥ suvi̱tāya̍ gantana | i̱yaṁ vo̍ a̱smat prati̍ haryate ma̱tis tṛ̱ṣṇaje̱ na di̱va utsā̍ uda̱nyave̍ ||
2vāśī̍manta ṛṣṭi̱manto̍ manī̱ṣiṇa̍ḥ su̱dhanvā̍na̱ iṣu̍manto niṣa̱ṅgiṇa̍ḥ | svaśvā̍ḥ stha su̱rathā̍ḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ svāyu̱dhā ma̍ruto yāthanā̱ śubha̍m ||
translation.text:
1OF one accord, with Indra, O ye Rudras, come borne on your golden car for our prosperity. An offering from us, this hymn is brought to you, as, unto one who th irsts for water, heavenly springs.
2Armed with your daggers, full of wisdom, armed with spears, armed with your quivers, armed with arrows, with good bows, Good horses and good cars have ye, O Pr̥iṣni's Sons: ye, Maruts, with good weapons go to victory.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 376v (numbered 49v by the scribe) (OPenn image 377, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.56.8 ‹tasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 377r (numbered 50r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.57.3 ‹vasu ni vaḥ vanā›. Verses 5.57.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.57.3-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 377r
translation.original_text:
3dhū̱nu̱tha dyām parva̍tān dā̱śuṣe̱ vasu̱ ni vo̱ vanā̍ jihate̱ yāma̍no bhi̱yā | ko̱paya̍tha pṛthi̱vīm pṛ̍śnimātaraḥ śu̱bhe yad u̍grā̱ḥ pṛṣa̍tī̱r ayu̍gdhvam ||
4vāta̍tviṣo ma̱ruto̍ va̱rṣani̍rṇijo ya̱mā i̍va̱ susa̍dṛśaḥ su̱peśa̍saḥ | pi̱śaṅgā̍śvā aru̱ṇāśvā̍ are̱pasa̱ḥ pratva̍kṣaso mahi̱nā dyaur i̍vo̱rava̍ḥ ||
5pu̱ru̱dra̱psā a̍ñji̱manta̍ḥ su̱dāna̍vas tve̱ṣasa̍ṁdṛśo anava̱bhrarā̍dhasaḥ | su̱jā̱tāso̍ ja̱nuṣā̍ ru̱kmava̍kṣaso di̱vo a̱rkā a̱mṛta̱ṁ nāma̍ bhejire ||
translation.text:
3From hills and heaven ye shake wealth for the worshipper: in terror at your coming low the woods bow down. Ye make the earth to tremble, Sons of Pr̥iṣni, when for victory ye have yoked, fierce Ones! your spotted deer.
4Bright with the blasts of wind, wrapped in their robes of rain, like twins of noble aspect and of lovely form, The Maruts, spotless, with steeds tawnyhued and red, strong in their mightiness and spreading wide like heaven.
5Rich in adornment, rich in drops, munificent, bright in their aspect, yielding bounties that endure, Noble by birth, adorned with gold upon their breasts, the Singers of the sky have won immortal fame.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.57.6-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 377v
translation.original_text:
6ṛ̱ṣṭayo̍ vo maruto̱ aṁsa̍yo̱r adhi̱ saha̱ ojo̍ bā̱hvor vo̱ bala̍ṁ hi̱tam | nṛ̱mṇā śī̱rṣasv āyu̍dhā̱ rathe̍ṣu vo̱ viśvā̍ va̱ḥ śrīr adhi̍ ta̱nūṣu̍ pipiśe ||
7goma̱d aśvā̍va̱d ratha̍vat su̱vīra̍ṁ ca̱ndrava̱d rādho̍ maruto dadā naḥ | praśa̍stiṁ naḥ kṛṇuta rudriyāso bhakṣī̱ya vo 'va̍so̱ daivya̍sya ||
8ha̱ye naro̱ maru̍to mṛ̱ḻatā̍ na̱s tuvī̍maghāso̱ amṛ̍tā̱ ṛta̍jñāḥ | satya̍śruta̱ḥ kava̍yo̱ yuvā̍no̱ bṛha̍dgirayo bṛ̱had u̱kṣamā̍ṇāḥ ||
translation.text:
6Borne on both shoulders, O ye Maruts, are your spears: within your arms is laid your energy and
7Vouchsafe to us, O Maruts, splendid bounty in cattle and in steeds, in cars and heroes. Children of Rudra, give us high distinction: may I enjoy your Godlike help and favour.
8Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures, Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.
